facts.detail: A reported total loss of fixed broadband or landline service qualifies after two full working days, at £10.34 for each calendar day unrepaired.
A missed engineer appointment, or cancellation with less than 24 hours' notice, attracts £32.31.
A delayed promised start of a new service attracts £6.46 for each calendar day of delay.
The voluntary scheme covers residential fixed broadband and landline products of participating providers.

guard_streams.write_limit: Compensation rights and amounts do not prove parcel coverage, speed or orderability.

facts.detail: Delayed-start and missed-appointment compensation is paid automatically without a separate claim.
For loss of service, the customer reports the fault once and automatic compensation begins if repair exceeds the two-working-day threshold.
Unless otherwise agreed, compensation is a bill credit due within 30 calendar days after resolution, termination, cancellation or the missed appointment.
Unless an exclusion applies, events outside either party's control, including extreme weather, strikes and third-party acts, can still qualify.

guard_streams.write_limit: Payment process evidence is customer-remedy evidence, not exact network availability.

facts.detail: Simultaneous loss of landline and broadband generates one compensation payment, not two.
Loss caused by equipment or activity inside the home is excluded.
Contract breach, customer-caused failure or customer prevention of timely resolution can exclude payment.
After 30 days of payments, a provider may issue a cease notice for a further 30 days and must take reasonable steps toward a suitable alternative service.

guard_streams.write_limit: Compensation exclusions and cease rules cannot be converted into parcel observations.

facts.detail: Vodafone, EE, Three and O2 have completed their UK 3G switch-offs.
All mobile network operators have confirmed 2G switch-off by 2033 at the latest, with earlier operator-specific dates possible.
EE has announced that its 2G switch-off will begin from May 2029.
VodafoneThree plans Vodafone 2G switch-off during 2030, while O2 plans to start in summer 2029.

guard_streams.write_limit: National switch-off schedules do not prove current parcel signal or service.

facts.detail: Most 4G or 5G devices are unlikely to be affected, though some may need software or settings updates.
A 2G-only phone or service must be upgraded to at least 4G before the relevant 2G network closes.
Providers should contact affected customers with notice, and may offer extra support for affordable replacement options.
Care alarms, security alarms, payment terminals and other connected devices may also require upgrading.

guard_streams.write_limit: Device compatibility and customer support do not establish parcel coverage.

facts.detail: Each mobile network operator is responsible for its own switch-off timing and process.
Ofcom expects customers to be treated fairly and to retain access to the services they need through the transition.
Providers remain subject to relevant regulatory requirements during network retirement.
A voluntary 2G switch-off charter was published in March 2026 to support a smooth transition.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regulatory expectations and operator timetables are not parcel-level evidence.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom IoT and third-party device switch-off advice

facts.detail: Affected categories include telecare, security and fire alarms, ATMs and payment terminals.
All 2G-only connected devices will need upgrading to at least 4G.
A supplier of a 2G-dependent service is responsible for planning continuity after switch-off, subject to contracts and regulation.
Suppliers using roaming SIMs must assess how domestic 2G changes and inbound-roaming restrictions affect their devices.

guard_streams.write_limit: Device-sector planning cannot be assigned as live connectivity to individual parcels.
